title: SLA-weighted Temporal Decay Opportunity Scorer
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Current RICE-style scoring in the roadmap treats Reach, Impact, Confidence, and Effort as static snapshots. This misses two important operational realities for Redwood: 1) features have different SLA/latency sensitivity (customer-facing low-latency features vs. batch/async jobs) which should amplify or attenuate priority based on contractual or product SLOs; 2) the opportunity value for some initiatives decays over time (market windows, seasonal launches, or competitive moves).

Goal: Design and roll out a prioritization extension that augments RICE with (a) an SLA-weight multiplier (captures how much latency/SLO risk the initiative affects) and (b) a temporal-decay function that reduces raw opportunity score as a function of roadmap cycles since idea validation. The output is a single score used in roadmap ordering and gating for commit/hand-off. The scorer must be explainable, easy to compute from existing inputs, and instrumented for retrospective validation against OKR outcomes and unit economics (token cost per DAU uplift).

Why this is different: Many existing documents focus on weighted RICE or cost curves. This ticket explicitly ties prioritization to contractual SLAs and time-decay windows and produces a gating score for cadence-driven rollouts (canary/cycle allocation). It aims to reduce rushed low-value launches to meet arbitrary dates and instead make opportunity/time trade-offs explicit to product and sales stakeholders.
acceptance_criteria: Scoring formula documented and reviewed in Roadmap Economics RFC (Confluence)
Implementation plan with required inputs from Console (SLA sensitivity per route) and Billing (token cost projections) is agreed and scheduled
Prototype sheet with sample initiatives computed across 3 quarters and a heatmap view validated by Growth and Enterprise PMs
Automation: script to compute scores from a CSV export of existing prioritization inputs; runs in CI and produces a ranked list
Instrumentation: key dashboards (score vs. outcome) created in Looker/Metriq and seeded with historical backtest for 18 past initiatives
decisions: Base formula: AdjustedScore = RICE_base * SLA_weight * Decay(t) where RICE_base = (Reach * Impact * Confidence) / Effort
SLA_weight: categorical mapping (critical SLO=1.25, sensitive=1.1, neutral=1.0, tolerant=0.9). Start with conservative multipliers to avoid over-amplification.
Decay(t): piecewise linear decay across cycles: t=0 (no decay), t=1 (0.85), t=2 (0.65), beyond 3 cycles clip at 0.4). Review coefficients after 2 cycles of live telemetry.
Customer-facing enterprise contracts will get a manual override flag (requires justification and sign-off from Sales Engineering and PM leadership).

Backtest: run scoring over historic initiatives and produce precision/recall vs. top-10 OKR outcomes
UX: small dashboard in Console to show score decomposition per initiative (PM + Strategy ownership)
Rollout: soft-launch for Cycle 2026-W11, mandatory for new initiative intake for three pilot teams (Growth, Enterprise, Platform)

comments: 2026-02-11 | Aisha Patel: Initial RFC posted. Requesting SMEs from Growth and Enterprise to review the SLA multiplier buckets. Opening data dependency tickets to Console and Billing.

2026-02-18 | Liam O'Connor: Completed export of 24 initiatives into prototype sheet. Early signal: Decay coefficients of 0.9/0.7/0.5 produced very few rank changes; increased steepness to proposed 0.85/0.65/0.4 for more separation.

2026-02-24 | Jenna Morales (Growth PM): Reviewed prototype. Concern — SLA multipliers may bias away from high-reach but latency-tolerant experiments. Proposed adding a normalization step that limits maximum multiplier effect to x1.3. Decision: keep multipliers conservative and cap overall SLA amplification at 1.25.

2026-03-01 | Marco Hsu (Sales Eng): Flagged that Enterprise contract renewals sometimes require date-driven launches; added request for manual override / gating workflow (sales justification) which is included in decisions.
2026-03-05 | Liam O'Connor: Opened prototype PR #17 with scoring script and CSV input schema. CI job added to validate inputs. See GitHub link.

2026-03-10 | Aisha Patel: Backtest completed on 18 prior initiatives. Preliminary result: adjusted score ranked top-decile initiatives that achieved >60% of expected OKR lift with precision 0.72. Added acceptance criterion to instrument dashboards for ongoing validation. Next: schedule cross-functional review 2026-03-15.
